_doc: Medium batch m07 themed pass (Opus): muskrats, capybaras, five frogs and toads, a snapping-turtle hatchling and four lizards. Every creature has its own signature motif (module claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m07.js, 38 motifs; four signatures bring a custom chain effect: muskrat swimming with a V wake, capybara plodding with its riding bird, bullfrog crossing in three leaps, basilisk sprinting on the water). Two small motifs are reused where truly the same: musk-wave (the zorilla's musk lines) for the muskrat's musk and croak-ring (the natterjack's throat rings) for the cane toad's croak. All 8 pieces per creature carry a hand note.

muskrat-crew.notes: A work gang of small dark muskrats with thin scaly tails: they swim low with a V wake, chisel reeds with orange teeth, build reed lodges and weave reed mats, and smell of musk.

u0.n: Lodge Wall: reed lodge domes build up along the edge layer by layer, mud packed between, a muskrat peeking from the door

u1.n: Reed Mat: woven reed mats pop out of the edge and drop back, the weave shifting

u2.n: Musk Gnaw: orange chisel teeth lunge off the edge and bite a reed through, a musk haze hanging

u3.n: Musk Cloud: wavy olive musk lines curl up off the edge and hang

b0.n: Lodge Builder Paw: muskrats swim off the edge towing reed strands, wakes spreading

b1.n: Reed Chisel Gnaw: orange incisors snap off the edge, cut reed tops tipping over

b2.n: Lodge Wall Guard: reed domes stand along the edge, straw and mud

b3.n: Work-Gang Shove: the crew shoves out of the edge in a line and drops back, bubbles

capybara-herd.notes: A big calm herd of barrel-bodied capybaras with little yellow birds riding on their backs; they plod, they float with only eyes, ears and nostrils above water, and nothing ever hurries them.

p.u0: Herd Shove: barrel-bodied capybaras plod off the edge one after another, the birds on their backs hopping up
p.u1: Calm Float: capybara heads float out with only eyes, ears and nostrils above water, calm rings spreading, and drift back

u2.n: Water Slap: floating capybaras hang at spots tied by splash lines, slapping the water

u3.n: Riding Birds: little yellow birds hop up off the backs and flutter upward, ticks in their beaks

b0.n: Placid Toe Swipe: a capybara leans off the edge and swipes, the bird barely looking up

b1.n: Bulk Herd Slam: the whole barrel slams out of the edge and drops back, dust thrown up

b2.n: Birdback Stance: capybaras stand along the edge, a bird on every back, hooves printing

b3.n: Unhurried Hip Nudge: a capybara nudges out sideways, slowly, and back

desert-spadefoot.notes: A round tan desert toad with a black horny spade on each hind foot: it shovels itself backwards into the sand, sleeps through the dry season and wakes all at once when the first rain falls.

u0.n: Spade Wall: black spade feet line the edge shovelling a sand wall up, grains flying

p.u1: Dig Down Bash: spade feet slam out of the edge and dig back in, sand sprayed

u2.n: Rain Croak: round toad heads pop up out of the sand as the rain falls, croak, and duck back

p.u3: Waking Rain: raindrops fall and round tan toads push up out of the wet sand and rise

b0.n: Sand-Rain Gulp: toad heads burst out of the sand off the edge, gulping the rain

b1.n: Wet Sand Lash: spade feet lash out sideways, wet sand flung

b2.n: Sand-Sleeper Hide: sleeping toads lie just under the sand along the edge, a mound, then two eyes

b3.n: First Rain Spit: the first drops fall off the edge, the toads spitting as they wake

bullfrog.notes: A big olive bullfrog of the bog with a yellow throat: it whips a long pink tongue, booms a deep croak from a huge throat sac, puffs itself up round and gulps anything that fits.

p.u0: Tongue Lash: broad bullfrog heads whip a long pink tongue off the edge, sticky tip first; the chain crosses in three big leaps

u1.n: Deep Croak: huge yellow throat sacs swell at spot after spot, deep croak bars rolling out

p.u2: Puff Up: bullfrogs along the edge puff up round, warts and yellow throats swelling

u3.n: Bog Gulp: a huge mouth slams out of the edge, gapes and gulps shut, bog bubbles rising

b0.n: Gulping Maw: wide mouths lunge off the edge one after another and gulp

b1.n: Hind-Leg Kick: long hind legs kick straight out of the edge, webbed feet spread

b2.n: Warty Skin Plate: puffed bullfrogs hold the edge, a wet sheen over the warts

b3.n: Hop Away Bellow: a throat sac booms and the frogs drop off the edge, toxic spots left behind

cane-toad.notes: A heavy dry warty cane toad with big bulging glands behind its eyes that squirt milky toxin; it sits on night roads under the moon and hops aside, never far.

p.u0: Gland Squirt: the big gland behind the eye bulges and squirts a milky jet that falls off the edge

u1.n: Hop Aside: heavy toads hop out over a dashed road line and thump back

u2.n: Warty Dodge: the dry warts swell and bristle out as the toad ducks

u3.n: Road Hop: toads hop from spot to spot along a night road under a moon glint

b0.n: Eye-Gland Spray: glands squirt milky jets straight off the edge

b1.n: Roadside Hop Crush: a toad slams down out of a hop and drops back, road dust

p.b2: Dry Warted Hide: dry warts swell along the edge, pale crowns and dark rims

b3.n: Nightroad Croak: throat rings pulse and drop off the edge under the moon

poison-dart-frog.notes: A tiny jewel-bright blue rainforest frog with black spots and yellow flashes: the colours are the warning, the skin is the poison, and gnomes tip their darts with it.

u0.n: Dart Skin: gnome-length darts bristle out of the edge, poison tips glistening

p.u1: Toxic Touch: jewel frogs hop off the edge and fall, poison beading on their skin

u2.n: Bright Warning: blue and yellow warning rings flash on and off at spot after spot

u3.n: Jewel Flash: a jewel frog blinks from leaf to leaf, a white glint at each landing

p.b0: Jewel-Bright Nip: jewel frogs dart off the edge and nip

b1.n: Sticky Flick: tiny frogs hop out and a sticky tongue flicks

p.b2: Warning Colours: warning rings line the edge, flashing blue and yellow

b3.n: Gnome-Length Dart: one poison dart flies the length of the edge

golden-mantella.notes: A tiny bright golden-orange frog of island rainforest moss: it gleams like marmalade, skips over moss cushions, and its bright skin is a warning.

p.u0: Gold Flick: tiny golden-orange frogs skip off the edge, a white gleam sliding over each back
p.u1: Moss Rest: moss cushions swell up and rise off the edge, a dew bead on top

u2.n: Bright Warn: the little frogs pop out gleaming as a warning and drop back

u3.n: Marmalade Spill: glossy orange marmalade blobs fly off the edge stretching sticky strings

b0.n: Marmalade Nip: gold frogs dart out and nip, wet dew flicked

b1.n: Moss Flick: clumps of moss are flicked off the edge

b2.n: Golden Sheen: golden frogs sit along the edge, a sheen sliding over them

b3.n: Spill Spray: marmalade drops stretch and fall off the edge

snapper-hatchling-bask.notes: Walnut-sized soft-shelled snapping-turtle hatchlings basking in a row on a log: hooked beaks that snap far above their size, an egg tooth still on the tip, mud stirred up when they slide in.

p.u0: Hatchling Snap: hatchlings lunge off the edge, necks shooting out, hooked beaks snapping
p.u1: Basking Log: a basking log holds the edge, hatchlings sitting on top and sliding off

u2.n: Mud Stir: murky mud swirls turn and sink off the edge

u3.n: Egg Tooth: a hatchling runs the edge beak first, the white egg tooth leading, eggshell crumbs breaking off

b0.n: Walnut-Sized Chomp: tiny shells pop off the edge, beaks chomping

b1.n: Log-Basking Flick: hatchlings flick off the log and out

b2.n: Soft Hatch Shell: soft ridged shells tuck in along the edge

b3.n: Single Bite Ploy: one hatchling drops off the log into the water and bites once, bubbles

sun-lizard.notes: A slim sand-gold lizard of hot stones: it basks flat in the sun, darts in a sprawl stride through the heat shimmer and drops its tail when caught.

p.u0: Sun Bask: a half sun with pulsing rays over a lizard lying flat, warm shimmer rising off the edge

u1.n: Tail Drop: a dropped tail wriggles out on its own and the lizard jerks back

p.u2: Lizard Dart: slim lizards dart off the edge in a sprawl stride, a glare flick behind

u3.n: Stone Snap: lizards snap from hot stones and drop off the edge, venom and grit falling

b0.n: Sun-Stone Bite: lizards dart off a hot stone and bite, dust kicked

b1.n: Dart Tail Whip: tails whip off the edge in an S

p.b2: Sun-Warm Scales: sun-warmed lizards lie along the edge under pulsing rays

b3.n: Dart Venom Spit: lizards dart and spit, venom spots dropping off the edge

rock-agama.notes: A blue-grey mountain agama with a bright orange head: it does push-ups on warm rocks to show off, then presses itself flat against the stone and vanishes.

p.u0: Head Bob Stab: an orange-headed agama runs the edge doing push-ups, the head bobbing down into a stab
p.u1: Rock Flatten: agamas press flat on warm slabs along the edge, only the orange heads showing

u2.n: Dart Tail: agamas dart off the ledge, venom specks dropping

u3.n: Warm Rock Bask: warm slabs rise off the edge, a heat haze shimmering over the flattened agamas

b0.n: Bobbing Snapjaw: agamas bob out of the edge and snap

b1.n: Warm Rock Whip: agamas whip off their warm slabs

b2.n: Sunbaked Scale Wall: sunbaked slabs line the edge, agamas flat on them, grit drifting

b3.n: Ledge Spitter: agamas push up on the ledge and spit, grit falling off the edge

basilisk-runner.notes: A green rainforest basilisk with a tall crest and very long toes: it rears up and sprints across the water on its hind legs, a splash at every step.

p.u0: Run Strike: basilisks rear up and sprint off the edge on their hind legs, a splash at every footfall; the chain runs along the water
p.u1: Crest Rest: tall crest sails ripple and rise off the edge

u2.n: Splash Cover: long toes slap the water along the edge, a curtain of splash drops kicked up

u3.n: Toe Skim: the runner skims across the water from spot to spot

b0.n: Hindleg Jaw Lunge: a basilisk lunges out upright and snaps

b1.n: Pond-Skid Whip: toes skid off the edge, splash fans thrown

p.b2: Crest Fan Shield: crest sails stand along the edge, rippling

b3.n: Stilt-Run Spray: splash drops kicked off the edge rain down

frilled-lizard.notes: A brown dry-forest lizard with a huge collar: when cornered it snaps the frill open like an umbrella round a gaping yellow mouth, hisses, and fans the dust.

p.u0: Frill Flare: the huge ribbed collar snaps open like an umbrella round a gaping mouth, bristling out of the edge

u1.n: Ruff Bite: gaping heads lunge off the edge and bite, venom dripping as they fall

u2.n: Dust Fan: the collar fans a brown dust cloud out and folds back

u3.n: Second Hiss: the gaping yellow mouth slams out with an S hiss and drops back

b0.n: Bluffing Gape: gaping mouths lunge out one after another, hissing

b1.n: Hiss Tail Flick: collars flare as the lizards flick off the edge

b2.n: Dinner-Plate Collar: open collars stand along the edge like dinner plates

b3.n: Hiss Warning Spit: a gape hisses and spit drops fall off the edge
